Subject: FinEx — Post-call: throughput & SLO qualification (recap & next steps)

Sam — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our discovery and the follow-up items we discussed. Please flag anything we misread:

Summary of perf targets and workload characteristics discussed:
- Latency SLOs: 95th percentile for user-facing streaming responses <= 300 ms (ideal target 250 ms) for typical response sizes (~125 tokens).
- Throughput: steady-state ~5,000 tokens/sec across the service; expected peak bursts up to ~10,000 tokens/sec during marketing spikes.
- Concurrency / QPS: typical concurrency 30-50 concurrent streaming sessions; peak concurrency up to 120; average QPS ~40 reqs/sec, peak QPS ~120 reqs/sec.
- Tokens per request: median ~125 tokens, 95th ~600 tokens for long-form workflows.
- Streaming: required — partial token streaming (SSE/WebSocket) and the ability to resume/continue truncated responses.
- Persistence/Retention: not yet finalized — you mentioned short audit logs for 30 days.

Next steps (our proposed plan):
1) Neha will build a throughput-sizing workbook with two scenarios (conservative peak and steady-state) and initial GPU sizing/expected cost.
2) We'll return assumptions on batching, quantization (INT8 candidate), and recommended routing (single model with fallback to smaller variant).
3) Provide a short attachment with the post-call notes and a sample sizing workbook (attached).

Can you confirm: the 95th latency SLO should be applied to streaming first-byte latency or end-to-end full response? Also confirm peak concurrency window — is that a sustained 10-15 minute window or shorter bursts?

Thanks — looping Neha + Marissa to take action.

— Rafael

Thanks Rafael — this looks right. A few clarifications:

- Latency SLO: aim for 95th on end-to-end streaming latency (time to first streamed tokens matters most, but we also care about completion latency for longer responses). If you can give both first-byte and end-to-end numbers that'd be ideal.
- Peak concurrency: the 120 figure is a hard peak we've seen during promotions but it's usually a short burst (2-5 minutes). The 30-50 range is our sustained business-hour concurrency.
- Streaming: we use SSE for the webapp; client expects incremental tokens and the ability to cancel/restart without incurring a new cold-start penalty.
- Cost: we care about cost per active session / per 1M tokens. If you can include rough cost deltas for quantized vs FP16 runs that would help procurement.

Also attaching a short file from engineering with sample payload sizes — I'll upload to the Drive link below this thread by EOD.

Hi all — attaching the initial throughput sizing workbook and the assumptions tab. High-level highlights below; details are in the workbook (attached).

Attachments: throughput_sizing_finex_v1.xlsx

Sizing summary (two scenarios):
- Steady-state scenario:
  - Avg tokens/sec: 5,000
  - Avg QPS: 40
  - Concurrency: 30-50
  - Assumed tokens/request: median 125
  - Suggested infra: 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs with batching and prefix caching (estimated sustained throughput ~6,000 tokens/sec, 95th latency ~220 ms FP16 with moderate batching).
- Conservative peak-burst scenario:
  - Peak tokens/sec: 10,000 (2-5 min bursts)
  - Peak QPS: 120
  - Peak concurrency: up to 120
  - Suggested infra for headroom: add 2 extra GPUs (total 6) + autoscale policy for burst capacity, or offload bursts to a cheaper quantized fleet (INT8) with slightly higher completion latency (~280-320 ms).

Cost delta (rough): FP16 baseline vs INT8 quantized fleet: ~20-35% cost savings on per-token compute, depending on model and kernel support. Network and storage not included in compute estimate.

Streaming: recommended approach is continuous KV caching + incremental token streaming (SSE). To avoid cold-start penalty on restart/cancel we recommend a short-lived prefix cache (30-60s) per session and immediate routing to fallback model if primary saturated.

Link to workbook: https://drive.google.com/finex/throughput-sample-v1

Next steps: Rafael — happy to do a quick walkthrough of the workbook and assumptions (15-30m). I can also add an additional tab modeling cost per 1M tokens for FP16 vs INT8 across the two scenarios.

— Neha Kapoor
